title: Linking through student ID
description: Student ID is transmitted as part of the data flow, enabling linking of data to specific individuals across the system boundary.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique identifier within the educational system.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: The combination of student ID, course, and file reference can serve as quasi-identifiers that may link data to specific individuals when analyzed.
assumptions: The combination of these attributes is unique or near-unique to individuals.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The data flow processes identified information including student ID, course, file reference, and requesting role.
assumptions: Student ID directly identifies the data subject.

title: Processing of identifier
description: Student ID is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject being transmitted through the data flow.
assumptions: Student ID is a globally or locally unique identifier.

title: Processing of quasi-identifier
description: The combination of student ID, course, and file reference constitutes quasi-identifiers that can identify the data subject.
assumptions: The combination of these attributes is sufficiently unique to identify individuals.

title: Data propagation to grading service
description: Personal data is propagated from the Grades Portal to the Assignment & Grading Service where it may not be strictly needed for all processing activities.
assumptions: The grading service may have access to more data than functionally required.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Personal data is made accessible to the Assignment & Grading Service, a predetermined set of parties known at design time.
assumptions: The grading service is a known, static recipient of the data.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware that their submission data including file references and role information is being transmitted to the grading service.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate all data flows.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the quality of privacy notices and user consent mechanisms.

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Students may lack control over how their submission data is processed and shared with the grading service.
assumptions: No granular consent options for data sharing.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the consent and preference mechanisms in place.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The data flow may process more personal data than functionally needed for the grading submission process.
assumptions: Some data elements may be excessive for the stated purpose.
uncertainty_note: Requires detailed functional analysis to determine if all data elements are necessary.

title: Unique identifier linking through student ID
description: The assignment store contains student ID which is a unique identifier that can be used to link all stored assignment data to a specific student, enabling identification and tracking of individual submissions across the system.
assumptions: Student ID is globally unique within the educational system and accessible to authorized parties.

title: Processing of identified information via student ID
description: The system processes identified data containing student ID, which directly reveals the identity of the data subject (student) and enables direct identification without additional information.
assumptions: Student ID is stored in plaintext or can be easily decrypted/recovered.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in assignment metadata
description: The combination of student ID, course, and submission time creates quasi-identifiers that could potentially identify students, especially in smaller courses or when combined with external information.
assumptions: Course enrollment data and submission patterns are available for correlation.

title: Attributable evidence of assignment submission
description: The stored assignment file with student ID and submission time creates evidence that can be used to prevent a student from denying they submitted the assignment, supporting academic integrity but also creating attribution evidence.
assumptions: The data is stored with sufficient integrity controls to maintain its evidentiary value.

title: Extended data retention beyond functional need
description: Assignment files with student identifiers may be retained longer than functionally necessary for grading purposes, potentially exceeding the storage limitation principle.
assumptions: No clear retention policy exists or retention exceeds academic record requirements.

title: Student unawareness of data collection and storage
description: Students may not be fully aware that their assignment submissions, including student ID and submission time, are being stored in the assignment store, particularly if consent mechanisms are unclear.
assumptions: Privacy notices are not prominent or students do not read them carefully.

title: Lack of student control over data processing preferences
description: Students may not have the ability to set preferences regarding how their assignment data is processed, stored, or shared with other services.
assumptions: No granular consent or preference management system exists for assignment data.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The assignment store may process more personal data than functionally required for grading, including student ID and submission time which could be considered excessive for the core grading function.
assumptions: Data minimization is not explicitly enforced in the system design.

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Assignment data with student identifiers may be retained longer than necessary for the functional purpose of grading, potentially violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: Retention policies are not clearly defined or enforced.
